properties.description: Core-shell structure with crystalline nickel core and amorphous nickel oxide shell

nodes.name: Electrodeposition of crystalline Ni core
nodes.procedure: Electrodeposition on Cu foam electrode in aqueous solution of NiCl₂ under a potential of -1.2 V, forming crystalline Ni particles.
nodes.source_text: Fig. S13 Electrodeposition i-t curves of Cu foam electrode in solution of NiCl₂ (for preparing c-Ni@a-NiO)... sharp current peak... electrodeposition speed is very fast

nodes.name: Electrodeposition of amorphous Ni(OH)₂ shell
nodes.procedure: Electrodeposition on Cu foam electrode (with pre-deposited Ni) in aqueous solution of NiCl₂/TAA under a potential of -1.2 V, forming amorphous Ni(OH)₂ shell around crystalline Ni core.
nodes.source_text: Fig. S13 Electrodeposition i-t curves... NiCl₂/TAA (for preparing c-Ni@a-Ni(OH)₂)... flat current platform... slower electrodeposition speed

nodes.characterization_summary: CV at non-Faradaic overpotentials (0.045-0.145 V vs. RHE) at scan rates 10-100 mV s-1 used to estimate Cdl proportional to ECSA for all catalysts; specific capacitance of flat surface 40 μF cm-2 used for ECSA calculation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The cyclic voltammetry (CV) was used at non-Faradaic overpotentials as the means for estimating the effective electrochemical surface areas. The potential range of 0.045-0.145 V vs. RHE that tested at different scan rates (10, 20, 40, 60, 80 and 100 mV s-1) were chosen... therefore 40 μF cm-2 was used in the following calculations of the ECSA.
